newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria to make stock exchange shareholder company.
newsitem.headline: Austria to make stock exchange shareholder company.

text.p: Vienna stock exchange announced plans on Tuesday to form a shareholder company to manage all trading operations, so raising efficiency and cutting costs, and also introduce a market segment for smaller firms.
Finance Minister Viktor Klima and stock exchange president Gerhard Randa told a news conference that the new company, Wiener Boerse AG, should be in place by the summer of 1997.

Separately, small and medium size firms would be encouraged to list their shares in a new market segment that should start up at the beginning of next year. Klima forecast the first listings in the second quarter of 1997.
He said the changes were necessary to strengthen Vienna's position as a financial centre in an increasingly competitive European market.

"This is a reform to mark the turn of the century. We are turning the bourse into a shareholder company that will represent the interests of all market participants," Klima said after a stock exchange strategy group meeting.
He noted that the move to create a shareholder company brought Austria into line with Germany, Switzerland and the Netherlands.

"The creation of a shareholder company will unify the cash and futures markets, raise competitiveness, create clearly defined areas of responsibility and improve the service to customers," the stock exchange said in a statement.
Wiener Bourse AG would manage cash and OeTOB futures trading operations, data sales, technology, marketing and development and the new EQOS electronic trading system.
The state's stock exchange chamber (Boersekammer) would initially control 100 percent of the shareholder company but Randa forecast the eventual abolition of the state body.
"Our goal is to raise efficiency and costs...and raise market capitalisation," he said. ($1=10.64 Schilling)
